content:
sophie: @acme-rep hey — we're seeing a concentrated window of 429s tied to your API key. Can you paste one failing requestId and a short curl repro? :mag:

acme-rep: thanks. one example request id from our logs: rq_8b2f3a1c. We hit this at 2026-02-28T15:12:23Z. Our client logs show a burst of retries from three hosts. pasted headers from the failing response below.

acme-rep: ```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Sat, 28 Feb 2026 15:12:23 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
X-Request-Id: rq_8b2f3a1c
X-RateLimit-Limit: 120
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1709200343
Retry-After: 10

{"error":{"type":"rate_limit","message":"Rate limit exceeded"}}
```

acme-rep: curl we used to repro (removed API key):

acme-rep: ```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-large-1","input":"test"}'
```

jamal: thanks — that requestId is helpful. quick observations: header shows a token-bucket window of 120 (likely per-key short window). Remaining=0 matches an immediate 429. Can you also paste the client-side timeline for 60s around 15:12:00-15:13:00? need per-second counts from each host. even a small CSV is fine.

acme-rep: pasted per-host counts (requests/sec) we recorded:

acme-rep: ```
# timestamp, host_a, host_b, host_c
2026-02-28T15:11:55Z, 12, 8, 2
2026-02-28T15:12:05Z, 40, 30, 10
2026-02-28T15:12:15Z, 90, 60, 30
2026-02-28T15:12:23Z, 120, 50, 30  # 429s start
2026-02-28T15:12:30Z, 130, 55, 35  # retries ramping
2026-02-28T15:12:45Z, 50, 20, 10
```

jamal: that looks like a short burst that exceeded the 120 quota. couple of asks to fully repro:
- run the curl with `-i` (so we capture response headers) and paste both request + response (redact keys)
- run once with `-H "X-Request-Id: <uuid>"` so we can map to our logs (we can look up any rq_ id but this helps)
- if you can, produce a debug bundle: run your client with DEBUG=logging and collect the sequence around rq_8b2f3a1c and attach the log snippet.

arjun: adding infra context — looks like this is a per-key short window limit, not a global cluster limit. We throttle at the edge with a leaky-bucket per API key + short rolling window. Key thing: concurrent fanout across hosts + immediate retries will multiply token consumption.

arjun: suggestion: implement jittered backoff on 429s and cap client-side concurrency per API key to ~100 rps to start, then ramp. For immediate troubleshooting we can temporarily bump the quota on the key if this customer needs to resume traffic quickly (requires approval).

maria: @acme-rep if you want a quota bump we need the following: expected sustained rps, burst tolerance, billing contact, and confirmation you will implement retry/backoff. DM me the billing contact and desired numbers and I'll start the approval workflow.

acme-rep: understood — we'll add jitter and cap concurrency. before that, jamal, can you point to the exact server logs you need? we'll paste the bundle into this thread.

jamal: perfect. please paste the exact HTTP request (method+path+headers+body) and the full raw response (status+headers+body). if possible include: client timestamp, client ip, request id you sent (or ours), and any SDK retry metadata. Example of the command we want you to run (this will return headers in-band):

jamal: ```bash
# run once to capture raw headers/body
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -H "X-Request-Id: my-test-$(date +%s)" \n  -d '{"model":"gpt-large-1","input":"repro test"}'
```

jamal: once you paste that, we'll pull the internal trace for the X-Request-Id (or our rq_ id) and verify which throttle rule fired. deploy-bot: note — rate-limit alert for key ending with ...c47 (threshold: 120 rps) at 2026-02-28T15:12:23Z.

deploy-bot: [alert] key: ****c47 — short-window spike detected — auto-mitigation not enabled for this tier.

acme-rep: ok will run now and paste results. one more question — are quota windows sliding or fixed reset? we saw Reset header but not sure interpretation.

arjun: sliding/rolling window. X-RateLimit-Reset is an epoch for when the allowance will next be non-zero in the current rolling window; treat Retry-After as authoritative for clients. We'll annotate docs to be clearer.

sophie: thanks everyone — acme, once you paste the curl -i output + client timeline + one more requestId (if differs) we'll escalate to quota bump thread and propose mitigations. :white_check_mark:

acme-rep: pasted the curl output and logs in the thread (redacted). rq id from our run: my-test-1801234599, server responded with X-Request-Id: rq_8b2f3a1c again. attaching client timeline snippet.

jamal: received — I'll lookup internal trace and reply with which rule fired and a suggested short-term lift if needed. will post trace id in ~10m.

jamal: internal note: trace pulled. rule fired: per_key_short_window_v2. evidence: consecutive spikes from three IPs within 10s. recommended temporary mitigation: 30s 2x burst tolerance for key ****c47 pending customer's implementation of jitter/backoff.

sophie: closing loop — acme please confirm when you've added jitter and reduced concurrency; maria I'll follow up on quota approval if acme requests. thanks all.
